context_requirements: Expression of at least one adenosine receptor subtype (ADORA1, ADORA2A, ADORA2B, or ADORA3) on the cell surface
Adenosine tone or receptor activity sufficient for antagonist to reduce constitutive signaling
Intact downstream ERK/JNK or cAMP-PKA signaling for transcriptional and apoptotic effects
Cancer cell context permissive to growth arrest/apoptosis (e.g., bladder, esophageal, or other carcinoma lines)
falsifiers: No consistent change in proliferation or apoptosis markers at 24 h across multiple cell lines
Lack of any transcriptional response (kinetics 'none') in all nine lines
No modulation of immediate-early genes (FOS, JUN, EGR1) at 6 h in responsive lines
Absence of cell-cycle gene downregulation (e.g., CCND1, MYC, CDK1) at 24 h
No correlation between adenosine receptor expression and response magnitude across lines

evidence.supports: A3 adenosine receptor antagonist induces apoptosis and growth arrest in T24 bladder cancer cells via ERK/JNK
A1 adenosine receptor antagonist induces apoptosis via caspase-3/7 in esophageal cancer cell lines
Adenosine receptor overexpression in esophageal tumors; A2B antagonist inhibits adenosine-induced cell death
Caffeine as nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist modulates oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis in brain injury models
